correctness.rationale: The published inverse-probability SPPM-NS update becomes two explicitly computed strict affine contractions; coupled moments converge. Their exact rational steady-state error factors against 1/9 with polynomial F and a manifestly positive denominator. For fixed p, Descartes ensures a unique positive F zero. Bernstein negativity at gamma=2, compactness of the maximum and exact resultant lead to quintic P; its derivative and endpoints prove one positive root and every parameter-side assertion. Reproducibility script verified factorization, resultant, endpoints, rational witnesses and moment recurrences, but analytic proof supplies continuum validity.

Its rate/variance bound-optimizing choices concern different objectives. Ryu–Boyd gives general proximal iteration contraction without this probability-dependent terminal-risk classification. Searches of comparable published records identified no implication covering the new sharp boundary. Equivalence in unexamined literature is a documented residual risk, not ruled out.

value.rationale: The distinction between rate-optimal nonuniform stochastic sampling and terminal error is mathematically and computationally motivated in the exact SPPM-NS scheme. The theorem gives a natural all-probability classification on the minimal pair of heterogeneous strongly convex quadratics, including sharp loss of attainment at an excluded probability boundary. This is an informative reliability/selection boundary, not mere rounding of a known table; usefulness is limited to this stationary-risk setup.
